state:
- The ATP-sparing window is in tension with the packet: S2 defines the target residuals by elevated oxidative metabolism, and S1 withholds any therapeutic-window claim from mitochondrial inhibition. Prespecify a same-cell CoQ-reduction titration relating dihydroorotate:orotate rise to ATP, and treat pyrimidine suppression only at energetic collapse as falsifying the selective window.
- S2 fatty-acid oxidation and approved direct DHODH inhibitors (leflunomide/teriflunomide; approval and exposure still need verification) are missing as competing arms, so an atovaquone effect can be mis-assigned to indirect DHODH restriction. Run both at unbound clinical exposure and abandon atovaquone if either accounts for maturation or if atovaquone fails to separate pool loss from ATP loss.
- Stacked gates (OCR fold-change, ≤25% salvage, immaturity, brequinar response) plus inducible Ura1 in primary residuals let the claim survive by sample exclusion, and primary residual cells rarely support that genetic rescue. Set a minimum qualification rate whose breach falsifies translational relevance, confine Ura1 rescue to an engineered AML model, and keep uridine rescue as the primary-specimen discriminator.
